sentences.en: In 2011, the body of a woman was discovered in a California vineyard.
sentences.zh: 2011年，一名女性的遗体在加利福尼亚州的一个葡萄园中被发现。

sentences.en: She had been decapitated, and her body had been drained of blood.
sentences.zh: 她遭到斩首，体内血液已被放干。

sentences.en: It appeared her killer had gone to extraordinary lengths to conceal her identity.
sentences.zh: 凶手似乎费尽心机，试图掩盖她的身份。

sentences.en: For more than a decade, she was known only as Jane Doe.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，她一直被称为“无名氏”。

sentences.en: Then, detectives finally learned her name, Ada.
sentences.zh: 直到后来，侦探们终于查明了她的名字：艾达。

sentences.en: But, identifying her only made this bizarre murder even more perplexing.
sentences.zh: 然而，确认她的身份反而让这起离奇的谋杀案变得更加扑朔迷离。

sentences.en: Ada is the new series from Casefile Presents, available now wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 《艾达》是Casefile Presents推出的全新系列节目，现已在各大播客平台上线。

sentences.en: Silk Road was an ancient network of trade routes that started in China in the 2nd century BC.
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路是一条古老的贸易路线网络，始于公元前2世纪的中国。

sentences.en: Via a combination of roads and sea routes, goods like silk, paper, and spices were transported from the producers in Asia to markets in Europe.
sentences.zh: 通过陆路和海路的结合，丝绸、纸张和香料等商品从亚洲的生产者手中被运往欧洲市场。

sentences.en: Eventually, it wasn't just goods that were traded.
sentences.zh: 最终，贸易的不仅仅是商品。

sentences.en: There were also ideas, customs, religions, and even diseases.
sentences.zh: 还有思想、习俗、宗教，甚至是疾病。

sentences.en: The Silk Road expanded throughout different continents and civilizations for several centuries.
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路在几个世纪里不断扩张，横跨了不同的洲和文明。

sentences.en: It connected Asia, Europe, Africa, and the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 它连接了亚洲、欧洲、非洲和中东。

sentences.en: A marketplace across the world.
sentences.zh: 一个全球性的市场。

sentences.en: Two major expansions can be traced back to the Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路可以追溯到两次重大的扩张。

sentences.en: One of these was the introduction of Buddhism into China.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是佛教传入中国。

sentences.en: The second was the Black Death.
sentences.zh: 第二次则是黑死病。

sentences.en: Vermin accompanied some of the goods along the Silk Road, and upon the vermin were fleas.
sentences.zh: 害虫随着丝绸之路上的某些货物一起传播，而跳蚤就寄生在这些害虫身上。

sentences.en: These fleas carried the bubonic plague, also known as the Black Death.
sentences.zh: 这些跳蚤携带了鼠疫杆菌，也就是所谓的黑死病。

sentences.en: And as the fleas entered Europe, so did the plague.
sentences.zh: 随着跳蚤进入欧洲，瘟疫也随之而来。

sentences.en: It's estimated that in the 14th century, between 100 and 125 million people died from the Black Death, reducing the world's population by somewhere between 30 and 60 percent.
sentences.zh: 据估计，在14世纪，黑死病导致1亿至1.25亿人死亡，使世界人口减少了30%到60%。

sentences.en: The Silk Road is recognized as the very first true globalization that the world experienced.
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路被公认为世界经历的第一次真正的全球化。

sentences.en: The free trade of goods and the passing of ideas and customs from one society to another.
sentences.zh: 商品自由贸易以及思想和习俗在不同社会之间的传播。

sentences.en: It changed everything.
sentences.zh: 它改变了一切。

sentences.en: It would be many centuries later that a very different kind of marketplace would open up on a modern platform.
sentences.zh: 许多世纪之后，一种截然不同的市场将在现代平台上开启。

sentences.en: A new trade route, using the same name.
sentences.zh: 一条沿用相同名称的新贸易路线。

sentences.en: Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路。

sentences.en: Ross William Ulbricht was born on March 27th, 1984, in Austin, Texas.
sentences.zh: 罗斯·威廉·乌布利希于1984年3月27日出生在德克萨斯州奥斯汀市。

sentences.en: From a young age, he was described as social, curious, kind, helpful, and resourceful.
sentences.zh: 从小，他就被描述为一个善于社交、好奇心强、善良、乐于助人且足智多谋的孩子。

sentences.en: He joined the Boy Scouts and got to the rank of Eagle Scout, just like his father had.
sentences.zh: 他加入了童子军，并像他父亲一样获得了“鹰级童军”的称号。

sentences.en: After school, Ross earned a full scholarship to study physics at the University of Texas in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 高中毕业后，罗斯获得了全额奖学金，前往德克萨斯大学达拉斯分校攻读物理学。

sentences.en: He fell in love with a girl at university, and at the time of his graduation in 2006, he proposed to her.
sentences.zh: 他在大学里爱上了一个女孩，并在2006年毕业时向她求婚。

sentences.en: But his girlfriend confessed that she'd been seeing various other men on the side, and all plans for a wedding were called off.
sentences.zh: 但女友坦白说她私下里还和其他男人来往，于是所有的婚礼计划都被取消了。

sentences.en: Ross returned to his hometown and tried to figure out what to do with his life.
sentences.zh: 罗斯回到家乡，试图思考自己的人生方向。

sentences.en: He tried out for the Amazing Race television show with his sister, and when that didn't work out, he decided to continue with his studies.
sentences.zh: 他曾和姐姐一起报名参加电视节目《极速前进》，但没能成功，于是他决定继续深造。

sentences.en: He applied for a master's degree at Pennsylvania State University, and once again, he got a full scholarship.
sentences.zh: 他申请了宾夕法尼亚州立大学的硕士学位，并再次获得了全额奖学金。

sentences.en: His focus was on material science and engineering.
sentences.zh: 他的研究重点是材料科学与工程。

sentences.en: Up to that point, Ross was deeply interested in mathematics, science, and nature.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，罗斯对数学、科学和自然有着浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: But at Penn State, his interests shifted dramatically.
sentences.zh: 但在宾州州立大学，他的兴趣发生了巨大的转变。

sentences.en: He joined a club that explored a subject that fascinated him to no end.
sentences.zh: 他加入了一个社团，探索了一个让他着迷不已的主题。

sentences.en: Libertarianism.
sentences.zh: 自由意志主义。

sentences.en: Libertarianism is based on the concept that everything a person does should be up to them, not anyone else.
sentences.zh: 自由意志主义基于这样一个概念：一个人所做的一切都应由自己决定，而不是由他人决定。

sentences.en: Essentially, it advocates minimal government intervention in the lives of its citizens.
sentences.zh: 本质上，它主张政府应尽量减少对公民生活的干预。

sentences.en: Ross was especially interested in the theories of Ludwig von Mises and the Austrian School of Economics,
sentences.zh: 罗斯对路德维希·冯·米塞斯和奥地利经济学派的理论特别感兴趣，

sentences.en: which support the view that people are their own rulers and don't need a government to regulate them.
sentences.zh: 这些理论支持人们是自己主宰者，不需要政府来监管的观点。

sentences.en: Ross adopted a very different lifestyle because of this new intereSt.
sentences.zh: 因为这种新兴趣，罗斯采取了一种非常不同的生活方式。

sentences.en: He moved into a basement because he got it for free, and he got his clothes for free from a friend that handled a second-hand store.
sentences.zh: 他搬进了一个地下室，因为那是免费的；他的衣服也是从一个经营二手店的朋友那里免费拿来的。

sentences.en: Ross's idea was to see if he could live with nothing more than the necessities, a less materialistic life.
sentences.zh: 罗斯的想法是看看自己是否能只靠必需品生活，过一种去物质化的生活。

sentences.en: Ross was also a part of other clubs at Penn State.
sentences.zh: 罗斯在宾州州立大学还参加了其他社团。

sentences.en: One of them was an African drumming club.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是非洲鼓乐社。

sentences.en: During one of the club's get-togethers, he met a fellow student by the name of Julia.
sentences.zh: 在社团的一次聚会中，他遇到了名叫朱莉娅的同学。

sentences.en: Julia was 18 years old at the time, six years younger than Ross.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅当时18岁，比罗斯小六岁。

sentences.en: Julia and Ross's time together is outlined in the book American Kingpin by Nick Bilden.
sentences.zh: 尼克·比尔登在《美国头目》一书中概述了朱莉娅和罗斯在一起的时光。

sentences.en: She remembered seeing Ross and thinking he looked homeless, with his torn-up clothes and unkempt beard.
sentences.zh: 她记得第一次见到罗斯时，觉得他看起来像个流浪汉，穿着破烂的衣服，留着邋遢的胡子。

sentences.en: Ross struck up a conversation with Julia, and one week later, they saw each other again.
sentences.zh: 罗斯主动与朱莉娅搭话，一周后，他们又见面了。

sentences.en: This time, Ross had shaved his beard and was dressed more presentably.
sentences.zh: 这一次，罗斯刮掉了胡子，打扮得体面多了。

sentences.en: He asked Julia out, and she agreed.
sentences.zh: 他约朱莉娅出去，她答应了。

sentences.en: They went out for dinner, after which they ended up back at Ross's basement, where Julia saw how he lived.
sentences.zh: 他们一起吃了晚饭，之后回到了罗斯的地下室，朱莉娅在那里看到了他的生活方式。

sentences.en: When she asked him about his less materialistic lifestyle, Ross explained that he was part of a libertarian club, and he was experimenting.
sentences.zh: 当她问起他这种去物质化的生活方式时，罗斯解释说他参加了一个自由意志主义社团，正在进行实验。

sentences.en: Julia didn't quite understand what libertarianism was, and Ross explained the basic concept.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅不太理解什么是自由意志主义，罗斯便解释了基本概念。

sentences.en: He used drugs as an example.
sentences.zh: 他以毒品为例。

sentences.en: Anything a person decides to put into their body should be their decision, and no one else's.
sentences.zh: 一个人决定往自己身体里摄入什么，都应该是他们自己的决定，而不应是别人的。

sentences.en: Especially not the government's.
sentences.zh: 尤其是政府的。

sentences.en: Ross's fascination with libertarianism continued, and he participated in a debate about whether drugs should be legalised or not.
sentences.zh: 罗斯对自由意志主义的痴迷持续增长，他参加了一场关于毒品是否应该合法化的辩论。

sentences.en: Ross defended the position that every person should have the free will to decide whether to take drugs.
sentences.zh: 罗斯捍卫的立场是：每个人都应该有自由意志来决定是否吸食毒品。

sentences.en: He said that many problems would stop if drugs were legalised, such as violence and turf wars, and the issue of poor quality drugs being cut with poison and dangerous chemicals.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果毒品合法化，许多问题就会消失，比如暴力、地盘争夺，以及劣质毒品中掺杂毒药和危险化学品的问题。

sentences.en: Ross's belief was that if drugs were legal, it would be safer for everyone.
sentences.zh: 罗斯的信念是，如果毒品合法，对每个人来说都会更安全。

sentences.en: After graduating from university, Ross decided that he had no interest in pursuing a career in science.
sentences.zh: 大学毕业后，罗斯决定他对从事科学事业毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: What he wanted to do was become an entrepreneur, and develop his own business.
sentences.zh: 他想成为一名企业家，发展自己的事业。

sentences.en: For a couple of years, he'd been thinking of ways to put his libertarianism ideals into action.
sentences.zh: 几年来，他一直在思考如何将自己的自由意志主义理想付诸实践。

sentences.en: The closest he'd come was the design of a seastead, a permanent dwelling based at sea, outside the regulation of any government.
sentences.zh: 他最接近的一次尝试是设计一个“海上家园”，一个位于公海、不受任何政府监管的永久性住所。

sentences.en: As much as he liked the idea, it would be hard to turn into a reality.
sentences.zh: 尽管他很喜欢这个想法，但要将其变为现实却很难。

sentences.en: But Ross found a workaround.
sentences.zh: 但罗斯找到了变通方法。

sentences.en: He'd always been a keen computer user.
sentences.zh: 他一直是个热衷于使用电脑的人。

sentences.en: Even when he decided to live a less materialistic life, he always had his laptop close by.
sentences.zh: 即使在决定过一种去物质化的生活时，他也总是随身带着笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: Most of his income came from computer-generated work.
sentences.zh: 他大部分收入来自电脑生成的工作。

sentences.en: He'd searched for odd jobs on Craigslist, and he'd entered a partnership with a friend to run a used book website called Goodwagon Books.
sentences.zh: 他曾在Craigslist上寻找零工，并与朋友合伙经营一个名为Goodwagon Books的二手书网站。

sentences.en: Ross was always on his laptop, and it was through his computer that he found a way to turn his seastead idea into reality.
sentences.zh: 罗斯总是守着他的笔记本电脑，正是通过电脑，他找到了将海上家园构想变为现实的方法。

sentences.en: At the end of 2009, Ross started talking with someone online that had the pseudonym Arto.
sentences.zh: 2009年底，罗斯开始在网上与一个化名为“阿尔托”的人交谈。

sentences.en: Ross found Arto on a forum on a libertarian website, and they started chatting via email.
sentences.zh: 罗斯在一个自由意志主义网站的论坛上发现了阿尔托，他们开始通过电子邮件聊天。

sentences.en: Ross wondered if he could create his free trade market idea on the internet and make it untraceable, outside the control and regulations of the government.
sentences.zh: 罗斯想知道是否可以在互联网上创建他的自由贸易市场构想，并使其无法追踪，脱离政府的控制和监管。

sentences.en: He discussed his idea with Arto, and Arto's held him that there was a way to create a website that couldn't be traced by the government, and the way to do it was through Tor.
sentences.zh: 他与阿尔托讨论了这个想法，阿尔托告诉他，有一种方法可以创建一个无法被政府追踪的网站，而实现这一目标的方法就是通过Tor。

sentences.en: Tor allows you to enter the deep web.
sentences.zh: Tor允许你进入深网。

sentences.en: The deep web is essentially the internet in its entirety.
sentences.zh: 深网本质上是整个互联网的全部。

sentences.en: The deep web is a part of the internet that is difficult to access.
sentences.zh: 深网是互联网中难以访问的一部分。

sentences.en: No one really knows how much content is available in the deep web, but a lot remains hidden there.
sentences.zh: 没有人真正知道深网中有多少内容，但其中隐藏着大量信息。

sentences.en: You can't use a search engine to get there, you can't use a normal web browser, and you can't just type in a normal web address.
sentences.zh: 你无法使用搜索引擎到达那里，无法使用普通的网络浏览器，也无法直接输入普通的网址。

sentences.en: In order to access the deep web, you do it through Tor, which is software that works as a web browser.
sentences.zh: 要访问深网，你需要通过Tor，这是一种作为网络浏览器运行的软件。

sentences.en: Tor was originally created by the US Navy.
sentences.zh: Tor最初是由美国海军创建的。

sentences.en: Its function was to protect communication inside the government.
sentences.zh: 其功能是保护政府内部的通信。

sentences.en: They wanted a way to communicate that couldn't be traced.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一种无法被追踪的通信方式。

sentences.en: So Tor was created.
sentences.zh: 于是Tor诞生了。

sentences.en: As Arto explained to Ross, Tor provides anonymity.
sentences.zh: 正如阿尔托向罗斯解释的那样，Tor提供了匿名性。

sentences.en: Once you enter Tor, you can't be traced, because your IP address and browsing history are hidden.
sentences.zh: 一旦进入Tor，你就无法被追踪，因为你的IP地址和浏览历史都被隐藏了。

sentences.en: An IP address is basically the identity of your computer.
sentences.zh: IP地址基本上就是你电脑的身份证明。

sentences.en: Whenever you connect to the internet, your computer is given a unique IP address.
sentences.zh: 每当你连接到互联网时，你的电脑都会被分配一个唯一的IP地址。

sentences.en: If someone knows your IP address, then you can be uniquely identified, and it may be possible to determine your location.
sentences.zh: 如果有人知道你的IP地址，那么你就可以被唯一识别，并且有可能确定你的位置。

sentences.en: When you enter the deep web, you need to know where you are going.
sentences.zh: 当你进入深网时，你需要知道你要去哪里。

sentences.en: It isn't like browsing Google.
sentences.zh: 它不像浏览谷歌那样简单。

sentences.en: It helps if you know the exact name and address of the site where you want to go.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道你想去的网站的确切名称和地址，会有所帮助。

sentences.en: And they aren't regular web addresses either.
sentences.zh: 而且它们也不是普通的网址。

sentences.en: Almost every site in the deep web uses mostly a random set of letters and numbers for its address, so it complicates matters even further.
sentences.zh: 深网中几乎每个网站的地址大多使用随机的字母和数字组合，这使得情况更加复杂。

sentences.en: Whilst the deep web has a reputation for being a place only used by hackers, hitmen, and child pornographers, there are many legitimate reasons for its use.
sentences.zh: 虽然深网因仅被黑客、杀手和儿童色情制作者使用而臭名昭著，但它有很多合法的使用理由。

sentences.en: Some of those are privacy, to avoid websites giving your data away to marketing companies.
sentences.zh: 其中一些包括隐私保护，以避免网站将你的数据泄露给营销公司。

sentences.en: People living in countries whose governments censor the internet can use it.
sentences.zh: 生活在政府审查互联网的国家的人们可以使用它。

sentences.en: Journalists use it to speak to sources and whistleblowers to assure anonymity.
sentences.zh: 记者使用它与消息来源和举报人交谈，以确保匿名性。

sentences.en: Ross thought the deep web sounded like the perfect place to create an anonymous website for his free trade marketplace idea.
sentences.zh: 罗斯认为深网听起来是为他的自由贸易市场构想创建一个匿名网站的完美场所。

sentences.en: But he still had a problem.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然有一个问题。

sentences.en: Even if he created a website where every person that entered was untraceable, he still needed an anonymous way of paying.
sentences.zh: 即使他创建了一个进入者都无法追踪的网站，他仍然需要一种匿名的支付方式。

sentences.en: If people had to pay with credit cards or PayPal, they could be easily traced, and the whole point would be loSt.
sentences.zh: 如果人们必须使用信用卡或PayPal支付，他们很容易被追踪到，那么整个意义就丧失了。

sentences.en: Ross asked Ardo about this.
sentences.zh: 罗斯向阿尔托询问了这个问题。

sentences.en: Ardo couldn't provide him with a straight-up solution, but he did tell him a story.
sentences.zh: 阿尔托无法直接提供解决方案，但他给罗斯讲了一个故事。

sentences.en: The story was the plot of a novel called A Lodging of Wayfaring Men.
sentences.zh: 这个故事是一部名为《流浪者旅店》的小说情节。

sentences.en: In the novel, there is a group of libertarians that want complete freedom from the government, so they create a virtual society and create their own digital currency.
sentences.zh: 在小说中，有一群自由意志主义者想要彻底摆脱政府的束缚，于是他们创建了一个虚拟社会，并创造了自己的数字货币。

sentences.en: The online society grows quickly, to the point where the government becomes afraid that the virtual society will destroy the norms of the actual society they live in.
sentences.zh: 这个在线社会迅速发展，以至于政府开始担心这个虚拟社会会摧毁他们所处的现实社会的规范。

sentences.en: Ross found the story interesting and inspiring, but he didn't know how to create his own digital currency.
sentences.zh: 罗斯觉得这个故事很有趣且富有启发性，但他不知道如何创造自己的数字货币。

sentences.en: It wasn't long until he found his solution, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，没过多久他就找到了解决方案。

sentences.en: Almost at the same time that Ross was having these discussions with Ardo about the deep web,
sentences.zh: 几乎就在罗斯与阿尔托讨论深网的同时，

sentences.en: Bitcoin was being created.
sentences.zh: 比特币诞生了。

sentences.en: Bitcoin is a decentralised cryptocurrency, a digital currency that exists only online.
sentences.zh: 比特币是一种去中心化的加密货币，一种只存在于线上的数字货币。

sentences.en: Like Ross, the creator of Bitcoin, someone going by the name or pseudonym Satoshi Nakamoto, wanted to get the banks and the government out of the way
sentences.zh: 和罗斯一样，比特币的创造者——一个化名为中本聪的人——想要摆脱银行和政府的干预，

sentences.en: so that people could freely make transfers of money with one another.
sentences.zh: 以便人们可以自由地进行资金转账。

sentences.en: Nakamoto started working on the creation of Bitcoin in 2007, and in 2008, the US suffered its biggest financial crisis since the Great Depression of the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 中本聪于2007年开始致力于比特币的创造，而2008年，美国遭遇了自1930年代大萧条以来最严重的金融危机。

sentences.en: Wall Street crashed, and the banks essentially lost everything, collapsing completely.
sentences.zh: 华尔街崩溃，银行几乎失去了一切，彻底倒闭。

sentences.en: Shortly after that happened,
sentences.zh: 在那之后不久，

sentences.en: Satoshi Nakamoto declared that a new currency was coming.
sentences.zh: 中本聪宣布一种新的货币即将到来。

sentences.en: Nakamoto posted on an online forum on February 11, 2009, on the Peer2Peer Foundation website.
sentences.zh: 2009年2月11日，中本聪在Peer2Peer基金会网站的一个在线论坛上发帖。

sentences.en: Quote,
sentences.zh: 引用如下：

sentences.en: The root problem with conventional currency is all the trust that's required to make it work.
sentences.zh: 传统货币的根本问题在于，它需要太多的信任才能运作。

sentences.en: The central bank must be trusted not to debase the currency.
sentences.zh: 必须信任中央银行不会让货币贬值。

sentences.en: But the history of fiat currencies is full of breaches of that truSt.
sentences.zh: 但法定货币的历史充满了对这种信任的背叛。

sentences.en: Banks must be trusted to hold our money and transfer it electronically.
sentences.zh: 必须信任银行能保管好我们的钱并进行电子转账。

sentences.en: But they lend it out in waves of credit bubbles with barely a fraction in reserve.
sentences.zh: 但它们却在信贷泡沫中大肆放贷，储备金却寥寥无几。

sentences.en: We have to trust them with our privacy.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在隐私方面信任它们。

sentences.en: Trust them not to let identity thieves drain our accounts.
sentences.zh: 信任它们不会让身份窃贼掏空我们的账户。

sentences.en: Their massive overhead costs make micropayments impossible.
sentences.zh: 它们高昂的间接成本使得小额支付变得不可能。

sentences.en: Nakamoto said that Bitcoin would solve all of these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 中本聪表示，比特币将解决所有这些问题。

sentences.en: The transfer of Bitcoin is made between one person and another.
sentences.zh: 比特币的转账是在人与人之间进行的。

sentences.en: No third participant or central figure is required to control it.
sentences.zh: 不需要第三方参与者或中心人物来控制它。

sentences.en: There are no taxes and no credits.
sentences.zh: 没有税收，也没有信贷。

sentences.en: Nakamoto's idea from the beginning was to make something straightforward.
sentences.zh: 中本聪从一开始的想法就是制造一种简单直接的东西。

sentences.en: A transfer without all the hassles that most currencies have nowadays.
sentences.zh: 一种没有当今大多数货币所具有的种种麻烦的转账方式。

sentences.en: A transfer that would be as simple as a person having something and giving it to another.
sentences.zh: 一种像一个人拥有某样东西并将其交给另一个人那样简单的转账。

sentences.en: Bitcoin managed to be exactly that.
sentences.zh: 比特币做到了这一点。

sentences.en: Bitcoin was exactly what Ross needed.
sentences.zh: 比特币正是罗斯所需要的。

sentences.en: Not only was Bitcoin created with similar ideals as his own, but it worked in a straightforward way.
sentences.zh: 比特币不仅创造理念与他自己的相似，而且运作方式简单直接。

sentences.en: A person could buy Bitcoins and manage them anonymously.
sentences.zh: 一个人可以购买比特币并匿名管理它们。

sentences.en: It's sort of like cash for the internet.
sentences.zh: 这有点像互联网上的现金。

sentences.en: It's hard to trace cash back to the person who spent it.
sentences.zh: 很难将现金追溯到花掉它的人身上。

sentences.en: When Bitcoin first appeared in 2010,
sentences.zh: 当比特币在2010年首次出现时，

sentences.en: Ross had been working tirelessly in the creation of his website for almost a year.
sentences.zh: 罗斯花了近一年时间，不知疲倦地创建着他的网站。

sentences.en: He taught himself programming and coding and made the website from scratch.
sentences.zh: 他自学了编程和代码，从零开始搭建了这个网站。

sentences.en: He didn't want anyone else to know about the site.
sentences.zh: 他不想让任何人知道这个网站的存在。

sentences.en: Because the first thing he wanted to solve it was drugs.
sentences.zh: 因为他想通过这个网站解决的第一件事就是毒品。

sentences.en: The only person he'd shared anything with up to that moment was Richard, a friend of his from the University of Texas.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，他唯一分享过任何信息的人是他在德克萨斯大学的朋友理查德。

sentences.en: Richard was a programmer and even though Ross had tried to learn as much as possible, he was only self-taught.
sentences.zh: 理查德是一名程序员，尽管罗斯尽其所能去学习，但他毕竟只是自学成才。

sentences.en: So when he got stuck with coding, he called Richard.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在代码上遇到困难时，他就会打电话给理查德。

sentences.en: When he shared the coding with Richard, he told him it was for a top-secret project and he didn't want any questions asked about it.
sentences.zh: 当他与理查德分享代码时，他告诉对方这是一个绝密项目，不希望对方问任何问题。

sentences.en: Richard respected the request and simply fixed the problem, having no idea what it was for.
sentences.zh: 理查德尊重了他的请求，只是修复了问题，完全不知道这是用来做什么的。

sentences.en: Ross did eventually share his website with his girlfriend, Julia.
sentences.zh: 罗斯最终还是把他的网站分享给了他的女朋友朱莉娅。

sentences.en: After they started their relationship at Penn State University,
sentences.zh: 在他们于宾夕法尼亚州立大学开始恋爱关系后，

sentences.en: Ross and Julia remained together through thick and thin.
sentences.zh: 罗斯和朱莉娅一直风雨同舟，不离不弃。

sentences.en: Julia didn't share Ross's passion for libertarianism, but she respected his views.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅并不像罗斯那样热衷于自由意志主义，但她尊重他的观点。

sentences.en: When Ross finished his master's degree and decided to become an entrepreneur,
sentences.zh: 当罗斯完成硕士学位并决定创业时，

sentences.en: Julia left Penn State with him and together they rented an apartment in Austin, Texas, his hometown.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅随他离开了宾夕法尼亚州立大学，两人一起在他家乡德克萨斯州奥斯汀租了一间公寓。

sentences.en: While Ross did several jobs,
sentences.zh: 当罗斯做着几份工作时，

sentences.en: Julia had her own photography business, Vivian's Muse.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅经营着她自己的摄影业务，名为“薇薇安的缪斯”。

sentences.en: Their apartment was her photography studio.
sentences.zh: 他们的公寓就是她的摄影工作室。

sentences.en: In November 2010, Ross blindfolded Julia.
sentences.zh: 2010年11月，罗斯蒙住了朱莉娅的眼睛。

sentences.en: She didn't understand what was happening, but allowed him to take her.
sentences.zh: 她不明白发生了什么，但还是任由他带她走。

sentences.en: He led her to his pickup truck and they drove for a while before coming to a stop.
sentences.zh: 他把她带到他的皮卡车上，他们开了一会儿车，然后停了下来。

sentences.en: Ross led Julia by her shoulders and when he finally took off her blindfold, all she saw was darkness.
sentences.zh: 罗斯扶着朱莉娅的肩膀，当他最终摘下她的眼罩时，她看到的只有黑暗。

sentences.en: She realised the only source of light was a small window and the place seemed small and had a strong odour.
sentences.zh: 她意识到唯一的光源是一个小窗户，这个地方看起来很小，而且有一股强烈的气味。

sentences.en: Julia was confused, but soon understood what was going on when Ross showed her a large shelf that had long trays of mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅感到困惑，但当罗斯向她展示了一个放着长托盘蘑菇的大架子时，她很快就明白了是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Magic mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 迷幻蘑菇。

sentences.en: Ross showed her each of the trays and explained that this was the place he'd been disappearing to recently.
sentences.zh: 罗斯向她展示了每一个托盘，并解释说这就是他最近经常消失去的地方。

sentences.en: The place was a small apartment he rented that was downstairs from the landlord's house.
sentences.zh: 这个地方是他租的一间小公寓，位于房东房子的楼下。

sentences.en: Ross was able to rent it without too many questions getting asked.
sentences.zh: 罗斯租下它时没遇到太多盘问。

sentences.en: He said he couldn't keep it to himself any longer.
sentences.zh: 他说他再也无法独自保守这个秘密了。

sentences.en: He had to tell someone and the blindfold was for Julia's own protection.
sentences.zh: 他必须告诉某个人，而蒙住眼睛是为了朱莉娅的安全着想。

sentences.en: What he was planning was big and if he got caught, he didn't want her involved.
sentences.zh: 他计划的事情规模很大，如果他被抓，他不想让她牵连其中。

sentences.en: After testing the quality of his mushrooms,
sentences.zh: 在测试了他的蘑菇质量后，

sentences.en: Ross felt it was time.
sentences.zh: 罗斯觉得时机到了。

sentences.en: In January 2011, the website was ready to launch.
sentences.zh: 2011年1月，网站准备上线。

sentences.en: He'd done the coding, the programming, the design and he'd created the first product to sell.
sentences.zh: 他完成了代码、编程、设计，并创造了第一个待售产品。

sentences.en: The choice of mushrooms to be the first thing to sell wasn't a surprising one.
sentences.zh: 选择蘑菇作为第一种销售商品并不令人意外。

sentences.en: Ross was a pro-drug advocate.
sentences.zh: 罗斯是一名毒品合法化倡导者。

sentences.en: His drugs of choice were marijuana, acid and psychedelics and he believed that if he was caught selling mushrooms, he would receive a lesser penalty
sentences.zh: 他偏好的毒品是大麻、迷幻药和致幻剂，他认为如果他因贩卖蘑菇被抓，受到的惩罚会比

sentences.en: than if he was caught dealing heroin or cocaine.
sentences.zh: 因贩卖海洛因或可卡因而受到的惩罚要轻。

sentences.en: The last thing Ross needed for his website was a name.
sentences.zh: 罗斯为他的网站需要的最后一件事是一个名字。

sentences.en: At one point, he was leaning towards underground brokers but at the last moment, he had a change of heart and went for a name that described not only the market
sentences.zh: 起初，他倾向于使用“地下经纪人”，但在最后一刻，他改变了主意，选择了一个不仅能描述市场，

sentences.en: but also emphasised the ideas behind it.
sentences.zh: 而且能强调其背后理念的名字。

sentences.en: That name was Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 那个名字就是“丝绸之路”。

sentences.en: When Ross launched the website, he shared it with only one person, his girlfriend, Julia.
sentences.zh: 当罗斯上线网站时，他只与一个人分享了它，那就是他的女朋友朱莉娅。

sentences.en: He'd already showed her the magic mushrooms and had given her a very quick summary of the website's idea.
sentences.zh: 他已经向她展示了迷幻蘑菇，并非常简要地向她介绍了网站的构思。

sentences.en: So when he opened the site for business, it made sense to show it to Julia.
sentences.zh: 所以当他正式开启网站业务时，向朱莉娅展示它是合情合理的。

sentences.en: He trusted her.
sentences.zh: 他信任她。

sentences.en: As outlined in the book
sentences.zh: 正如尼克·比尔顿在《美国大亨》一书中所述，

sentences.en: American Kingpin by Nick Bilton,
sentences.zh: 罗斯给了朱莉娅一份如何进入“丝绸之路”的分步指南。

sentences.en: Ross gave Julia a step-by-step guide on how to enter Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们在朱莉娅的MacBook上下载了Tor浏览器，

sentences.en: Once they had Tor downloaded on Julia's MacBook,
sentences.zh: 罗斯输入了以下地址：

sentences.en: Ross typed in the following address,
sentences.zh: 罗斯输入了以下地址，

sentences.en: tydg-ccyk-i-x-p-b-u6-u-z.onion.
sentences.zh: 这就是“丝绸之路”的网址。

sentences.en: This was Silk Road's web address.
sentences.zh: 因为它位于暗网，所以有一串随机的字母和数字，结尾是.onion而不是.com。

sentences.en: Because it was on the deep web, there was a bunch of random letters and numbers and ended with .onion instead of .com.
sentences.zh: 现在他们进入了“丝绸之路”，

sentences.en: Now that they were inside Silk Road,
sentences.zh: 罗斯让朱莉娅花点时间去消化这一切。

sentences.en: Ross allowed Julia time to take it all in.
sentences.zh: 她看到网站大部分是一个空白页面，上面用绿色写着“丝绸之路”的名字，旁边还有一个绿色的骆驼标志。

sentences.en: She saw the website was mostly a blank page with the name Silk Road written in green, along with the green logo of a camel.
sentences.zh: 这只骆驼是对现实中“丝绸之路”的致敬。

sentences.en: The camel was a reference to the actual Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 商人们过去常骑着骆驼穿越丝绸之路，因为许多路线位于沙漠和气候非常干燥的地方。

sentences.en: Merchants would travel through the Silk Road routes on camels because many were located in deserts and places with very dry weather.
sentences.zh: 但除了看到这些，

sentences.en: But other than seeing that,
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅不太确定如何浏览这个网站。

sentences.en: Julia wasn't too sure how to navigate the website.
sentences.zh: 于是罗斯继续解释。

sentences.en: So Ross continued explaining.
sentences.zh: 罗斯表现得像个普通买家，点击了网站内写着“毒品”的链接之一。

sentences.en: Ross acted like a regular buyer and went to one of the links inside the site that read drugs.
sentences.zh: 进入毒品分类后，还有另一个写着“致幻剂”的链接。

sentences.en: Once inside the drugs classification, there was another link that read psychedelics.
sentences.zh: 罗斯点击了那个链接，那里就是他的迷幻蘑菇，这是当时“丝绸之路”上第一个也是唯一可用的产品。

sentences.en: Ross clicked on that link and there were his magic mushrooms, the first and only product available on Silk Road at that point.
sentences.zh: 上面有一张图片展示了它们的样子以及价格。

sentences.en: There was a picture showing what they looked like and the price.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅问罗斯她该如何购买这些蘑菇，罗斯向她解释了比特币。

sentences.en: Julia asked Ross how she would go about buying the mushrooms and Ross explained Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 他给了她一个在游乐厅购买代币的例子。

sentences.en: He gave her the example of buying tokens in an arcade.
sentences.zh: 他告诉她，她会去游乐厅支付代币，然后用这些代币玩游戏，而没有人会知道她用了哪些代币。

sentences.en: He told her she'd go to the arcade and pay for tokens, which she could then use to play in the arcade and there would be no way of knowing which tokens she used.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅理解了这个概念，但不确定在哪里可以买到比特币。

sentences.en: Julia understood the concept but wasn't sure where to buy Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 于是罗斯去了一个比特币交易网站，要了她的信用卡。

sentences.en: So Ross went to a Bitcoin exchange site and asked for her credit card.
sentences.zh: 他输入了她的信息，就这样，她有了可以使用的比特币。

sentences.en: He entered her details and just like that, she had Bitcoins to use.
sentences.zh: 这个解释对朱莉娅来说似乎很简单，但她毕竟得到了网站创始人罗斯的亲自指导。

sentences.en: The explanation seemed simple enough to Julia but she'd received a guided explanation from Ross, the creator of the site.
sentences.zh: 所以她的下一个问题是，其他进入网站的人怎么知道该怎么做？

sentences.en: So her next question was, how would anyone else who entered the site know what to do?
sentences.zh: 罗斯向她展示了一份他为此编写的分步操作指南，这样买家和卖家就不会迷路。

sentences.en: Ross showed her a how-to step-by-step guide that he'd written for that purpose so that buyers and sellers wouldn't get loSt.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅脑海中的最后一个问题是，其他人怎么会知道“丝绸之路”的存在？

sentences.en: The last question on Julia's mind was, how would anyone else know about the existence of Silk Road?
sentences.zh: 罗斯通过向她展示他在不同网站上写的两篇帖子回答了朱莉娅。

sentences.en: Ross answered Julia by showing her two posts he'd written on different sites.
sentences.zh: 第一篇是他于2011年1月27日写的帖子。

sentences.en: The first one was a post he'd written on January 27, 2011.
sentences.zh: 他去了一个名为“蘑菇园”的迷幻蘑菇论坛，并以“Altoid”为化名注册了一个账户。

sentences.en: He'd gone to a Magic Mushrooms forum called The Shroomery and registered an account under the pseudonym Altoid.
sentences.zh: 注册后，他发布了以下信息。

sentences.en: After registering, he posted the following message.
sentences.zh: 引用：

sentences.en: Quote,
sentences.zh: 我偶然发现了这个叫“丝绸之路”的网站。

sentences.en: I came across this website called Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 它是一个Tor隐藏服务，声称允许你在网上匿名买卖任何东西。

sentences.en: It's a Tor hidden service that claims to allow you to buy and sell anything online anonymously.
sentences.zh: 我正考虑在上面买东西，但想看看这里有没有人听说过它，能不能推荐一下。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of buying off it but wanted to see if anyone here had heard of it and could recommend it.
sentences.zh: 我是通过silkroad420.wordpress.com找到它的，如果你有Tor浏览器，它会把你引导到真正的网站。

sentences.en: I found it through silkroad420.wordpress.com which if you have a Tor browser, directs you to the real site.
sentences.zh: 让我知道你们的想法。

sentences.en: Let me know what you think.
sentences.zh: 罗斯扮演了一个偶然浏览暗网并无意中发现该网站的角色，这样他就不会被认为是创始人。

sentences.en: Ross played the part of being someone who was casually browsing the deep web and came across the site by accident so he wouldn't be known as the creator.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他留下了进入“丝绸之路”所需的所有信息。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he left every piece of information one needed to enter Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 正如艾琳·奥姆斯比在《丝绸之路》一书中所述，他在普通互联网上创建的WordPress网站链接

sentences.en: As outlined in the book Silk Road by Eileen Ormsby, the link to the WordPress site that he created located on the regular internet
sentences.zh: 会将使用Tor浏览器的人重定向到暗网中的实际链接。

sentences.en: redirected people to the actual link in the deep web for anyone using a Tor browser.
sentences.zh: 在他创建的WordPress网站中，

sentences.en: In the WordPress site he created,
sentences.zh: 罗斯使用了“丝绸之路420”这个名字。

sentences.en: Ross used the name Silk Road 420.
sentences.zh: 数字420指的是4月20日，即官方的大麻日。

sentences.en: The number 420 refers to April 20th, the official day of marijuana.
sentences.zh: 当一个人进入该WordPress网站时，会出现一条消息说：这不是“丝绸之路”，但你已经很接近了。

sentences.en: When a person entered the WordPress site, a message appeared saying, this is not Silk Road, but you are close.
sentences.zh: 然后有一份关于如何下载Tor并访问暗网上实际“丝绸之路”网站的指南。

sentences.en: Then there was a guide on how to download Tor and access the actual Silk Road site on the deep web.
sentences.zh: 两天后，罗斯发布了关于“丝绸之路”的第二篇网络帖子，

sentences.en: Ross made a second web post about Silk Road two days later,
January 29th, 2011.
sentences.zh: 这第二篇帖子是在一个叫bitcointalk.org的网站上。

sentences.en: This second post was on a website called bitcointalk.org.
sentences.zh: 当时比特币还很新，人们正在讨论它的可行性及其可能的用途。

sentences.en: Bitcoin was very new at this point and people were discussing the viability of it and its possible uses.
sentences.zh: 一个看起来很有吸引力的用途是在暗网上支付商品。

sentences.en: One use that seemed attractive was to pay for things on the deep web.
sentences.zh: 罗斯发帖的那个特定论坛主题是关于使用比特币买卖海洛因的讨论。

sentences.en: The particular forum thread that Ross posted in was a discussion about using Bitcoin to buy and sell heroin.
sentences.zh: 罗斯的帖子写道：

sentences.en: Ross's post read,
sentences.zh: 引用：

sentences.en: Quote,
sentences.zh: 真是个很棒的主题。

sentences.en: What an awesome thread.
sentences.zh: 你们有很多很棒的想法。

sentences.en: You guys have a ton of great ideas.
sentences.zh: 有人见过“丝绸之路”吗？

sentences.en: Has anyone seen Silk Road yet?
sentences.zh: 它有点像一个匿名的亚马逊网站。

sentences.en: It's kind of like an anonymous Amazon.com.

sentences.zh: 很快，人们不仅访问“丝绸之路”进行买卖，他们自己也在推广这个网站。

sentences.en: Soon, not only were people visiting Silk Road to buy and sell, they themselves were promoting the site.
sentences.zh: 论坛上甚至在一个在线广播节目中开始出现讨论。

sentences.en: Once the purchase was made, the funds of the buyer would be retained by Silk Road in an escrow account until the buyer was satisfied with the purchase.

By April 2011,

sentences.en: During the first few weeks of operation, sellers offered mostly marijuana and psychedelics, like Ross himself was doing with his mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 但现在，卖家开始提供安非他命、可卡因和海洛因。

sentences.en: Julia believed that the consequences for Ross would now be much more severe if something happened to one of Silk Road's users or if he was caught by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 如果有人用药过量怎么办？

sentences.zh: 罗斯回答：

sentences.en: We have a rating system, so if someone sells bad drugs, they get a bad rating and no one will buy from them again.
sentences.zh: 我们有评分系统，所以如果有人卖劣质毒品，他们会得到差评，以后就没人会再买他们的东西了。

sentences.en: Ross was referring to a new feature he'd just added to Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 罗斯指的是他刚为“丝绸之路”添加的一项新功能。

sentences.en: When people bought or sold, they got good or bad feedback, just like eBay.
sentences.zh: 当人们进行买卖时，他们会像在 eBay 上一样获得好评或差评。

sentences.zh: 朱莉娅回应道：

sentences.en: How are they supposed to give someone a bad rating if they are dead?
sentences.zh: 如果人都死了，他们怎么给别人差评？

sentences.en: Julia also raised her concern about who was actually visiting the website.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅还提出了她对网站访客身份的担忧。

sentences.en: Neither her nor Ross expected Silk Road to grow as fast as it had, and it was only getting bigger by the day.
sentences.zh: 她和罗斯都没料到“丝绸之路”的发展速度会如此之快，而且规模还在与日俱增。

sentences.zh: 讨论的阵地从比特币论坛转移到了 4chan 和 Reddit 等网站。

sentences.en: At the end of May 2011, journalist Adrian Chen stumbled across several of these posts.
sentences.zh: 2011 年 5 月底，记者阿德里安·陈偶然发现了其中几篇帖子。

sentences.en: Chen wrote for Gawker, a well-known
sentences.zh: 陈为 Gawker 撰稿，这是一家总部位于纽约的知名

sentences.en: New York-based blogging and news media site.
sentences.zh: 博客和新闻媒体网站。

sentences.en: The site's main tagline was,
sentences.zh: 该网站的主要标语是：

sentences.en: Today's gossip is tomorrow's news.
sentences.zh: 今天的八卦就是明天的头条。

sentences.en: As detailed in the book
sentences.zh: 正如艾琳·奥姆斯比在《丝绸之路》一书中所详述的那样，

sentences.en: Silk Road by Aline Ormsby,
sentences.zh: 陈当时正在

sentences.en: Chen was on the
sentences.zh: 比特币论坛上，

sentences.en: Bitcoin Talk forum when he stumbled across a number of posts talking about Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 偶然发现了一些讨论“丝绸之路”的帖子。

sentences.en: At this point,
sentences.zh: 当时，

sentences.en: Bitcoin advocates were worried that Silk Road was giving Bitcoin a bad name as it was being promoted as the currency to pay for drugs on the dark web.
sentences.zh: 比特币的支持者们很担心“丝绸之路”会败坏比特币的名声，因为它被宣传为暗网上购买毒品的货币。

sentences.en: The more Adrian Chen read, the more sceptical he became.
sentences.zh: 阿德里安·陈读得越多，就越怀疑。

sentences.en: He found it hard to believe that there was a website where drugs could be sold so comfortably online.
sentences.zh: 他很难相信竟然有一个网站能如此轻松地在线销售毒品。

sentences.en: It seemed too easy.
sentences.zh: 这看起来太容易了。

sentences.en: Chen decided to follow the steps to enter Silk Road and as he browsed through the site, he saw that there were exactly 343 different listings of drugs with all sorts of variations.
sentences.zh: 陈决定按照步骤进入“丝绸之路”，当他浏览网站时，他看到上面竟然有 343 种不同的毒品列表，种类繁多。

sentences.en: The prices varied as well.
sentences.zh: 价格也各不相同。

sentences.en: There were drugs that were very expensive, others that were the same as street level prices and others that were cheaper.
sentences.zh: 有的毒品非常昂贵，有的和街头价格持平，还有的更便宜。

sentences.en: Chen believed there was definitely potential for a story but he still remained sceptical.
sentences.zh: 陈认为这绝对是一个有潜力的报道题材，但他仍然持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: He wanted to talk to someone who had actually bought drugs from the site.
sentences.zh: 他想找一个真正从该网站买过毒品的人谈谈。

sentences.en: He posted a message on the Bitcoin Talk forum stating he was going to write a story on Silk Road and he wanted to interview someone who had bought drugs there.
sentences.zh: 他在比特币论坛上发帖称，他打算写一篇关于“丝绸之路”的报道，并想采访一位在那里买过毒品的人。

sentences.en: Several people responded to Adrian's post detailing their experiences using Silk Road but he also got a response he wasn't expecting.
sentences.zh: 几个人回复了阿德里安的帖子，详细描述了他们使用“丝绸之路”的经历，但他还收到了一条意想不到的回复。

sentences.en: He got a response from Ross.
sentences.zh: 他收到了罗斯的回复。

sentences.en: Ross never revealed his true identity.
sentences.zh: 罗斯从未透露过他的真实身份。

sentences.en: He made a new account on the Bitcoin Talk forum under the name Silk Road to message Chen.
sentences.zh: 他在比特币论坛上以“丝绸之路”为名注册了一个新账号来给陈发消息。

sentences.en: Ross asked Chen to hold off on the story because Silk Road wanted to get bigger but wasn't ready for the attention quite yet.
sentences.zh: 罗斯要求陈推迟报道，因为“丝绸之路”还想做大，但还没准备好迎接关注。

sentences.en: Chen said he couldn't hold off.
sentences.zh: 陈说他无法推迟。

sentences.en: The story was going to be written now.
sentences.zh: 这篇报道现在就要写出来。

sentences.en: Unable to get the story shut down
sentences.zh: 无法阻止报道发布，

sentences.en: Ross decided to contribute to it.
sentences.zh: 罗斯决定参与其中。

sentences.en: He said that he was very proud of Silk Road and its community and he believed Silk Road was definitely making the purchase of drugs safer.
sentences.zh: 他说他为“丝绸之路”及其社区感到非常自豪，并相信“丝绸之路”绝对让购买毒品变得更安全了。

sentences.en: He ended with the following quote
sentences.zh: 他最后引用了这样一句话：

sentences.zh: 国家是暴力、压迫、盗窃和一切形式强制手段的主要来源。

sentences.en: Stop funding the state with your tax dollars and direct your productive energies into the black market.
sentences.zh: 停止用你的税款资助国家，将你的生产力投入到黑市中去。

sentences.zh: 陈在文中附上了各种在售毒品的照片以及网站本身的截图。

sentences.zh: 这篇文章火了。

sentences.zh: 数以百万计的人阅读了它。

sentences.en: Literally, it allows buyers and users to sell illegal drugs online, including heroin, cocaine and meth.
sentences.zh: 从字面上看，它允许买家和用户在网上销售非法毒品，包括海洛因、可卡因和冰毒。

sentences.zh: 它比其他任何东西都要猖狂得多。

sentences.zh: 通过立即打击该网站，我们可以帮助阻止这些毒品涌入我们的街道。

sentences.en: And because of that, no one ever knew who the original
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，没有人知道最初的

sentences.zh: Variety Jones告诉罗斯，

sentences.zh: 从管理员到“恐怖海盗罗伯茨”。

sentences.zh: 他说这样做的话，

sentences.zh: 罗斯就可以坚持他的说法，即他已经把网站转让给了别人，而他所知道的只是那个接手的人自称为

sentences.en: Dread Pirate Roberts.
sentences.zh: “恐怖海盗罗伯茨”。

sentences.en: Ross loved the idea, and on February 5th 2012,
sentences.zh: 罗斯很喜欢这个主意，于是在2012年2月5日，

sentences.zh: 丝绸之路管理员宣布他们将启用一个新的名字，

sentences.zh: “恐怖海盗罗伯茨”。

sentences.zh: 这个名字很快就大获成功。

sentences.en: The Silk Road community understood the reference to The Princess Bride and believed that it was indeed a perfect name on so many levels.
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路社区的人们理解这是对《公主新娘》的致敬，并认为在很多层面上这确实是一个完美的名字。

sentences.en: Most of Ross's employees, none of whom knew his real identity, started calling him Captain.
sentences.zh: 罗斯的大多数员工都不知道他的真实身份，开始称呼他为“船长”。

sentences.zh: 他的一位程序员告诉他：

sentences.zh: “我们真的可以改变世界。”

sentences.en: We are really lucky.
sentences.zh: “我们真的很幸运。”

sentences.en: This opportunity is on a scale of a few times in a millennia.
sentences.zh: “这种机会几千年才会有几次。”

sentences.en: All of his employees said that they had the same aim as Ross, to legalise drugs, and to ensure that future generations wouldn't spend their lives behind bars
sentences.zh: 他所有的员工都说他们和罗斯有着同样的目标，即让毒品合法化，并确保后代不会因为买卖或使用毒品而把一生浪费在铁窗之后。

sentences.zh: 2011年12月，毒品月销售额总计达到50万美元。

sentences.zh: 三个月后，即2012年3月，

sentences.zh: 毒品销售额已增加到每周50万美元。

sentences.en: Ross was making a lot of money with his 6.23% commission.
sentences.zh: 罗斯凭借他6.23%的佣金赚了很多钱。

sentences.en: But not everything was perfect.
sentences.zh: 但并非一切都尽善尽美。

sentences.en: There were problems in the community itself between buyers and sellers, involving loss packages and disputes with transactions.
sentences.zh: 社区内部买家和卖家之间存在问题，涉及包裹丢失和交易纠纷。

sentences.en: And it wasn't a secret that Silk Road's security was lacking.
sentences.zh: 而且丝绸之路的安全防范不足也不是什么秘密。

sentences.en: On one occasion, a hacker stole $75,000 worth of bitcoins from the site.
sentences.zh: 有一次，一名黑客从网站上窃取了价值7.5万美元的比特币。

sentences.en: Ross struggled to keep calm.
sentences.zh: 罗斯努力保持冷静。

sentences.en: He had a few panic attacks and he constantly bit his nails.
sentences.zh: 他经历了几次恐慌发作，并且不停地咬指甲。

sentences.en: He went on a holiday to Asia, but he told Variety Jones that he was unable to enjoy the trip at all.
sentences.zh: 他去亚洲度假，但他告诉“琼斯大杂烩”他根本无法享受这次旅行。

sentences.en: He had to constantly check on Silk Road no matter where he was and Wi-Fi wasn't the best where he visited.
sentences.zh: 无论身在何处，他都必须不断查看丝绸之路，而他去的地方Wi-Fi信号并不好。

sentences.en: Not only that, most of the places that had Wi-Fi were extremely busy and Ross had a rule.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，大多数有Wi-Fi的地方都极其拥挤，而罗斯有一条原则。

sentences.en: If someone could peer over his shoulder, he would move location so no one could see what he was doing.
sentences.zh: 如果有人能从他肩膀后窥视，他就会换个地方，这样就没人能看到他在做什么。

sentences.en: Something else that had added to his nerves was that some Asian countries had the death penalty for drug offences.
sentences.zh: 另一件让他神经紧绷的事情是，一些亚洲国家对毒品犯罪处以死刑。

sentences.en: So it wasn't a very relaxing holiday.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是一个非常放松的假期。

sentences.en: Ross returned to Australia after a month in Asia, after which he had a discussion with Variety Jones about the money they were making.
sentences.zh: 在亚洲待了一个月后，罗斯回到了澳大利亚，随后他与“琼斯大杂烩”讨论了他们赚的钱。

sentences.en: Variety Jones was estimating how much they would be making by the end of the year, but Ross interrupted him and said, that money won't be worth much if we're behind bars.
sentences.zh: “琼斯大杂烩”在估算他们年底能赚多少钱，但罗斯打断了他，说如果我们要坐牢，那些钱就没什么意义了。

sentences.en: Variety Jones said that they needed to come up with a plan.
sentences.zh: “琼斯大杂烩”说他们需要制定一个计划。

sentences.en: One of the first things they decided had to happen was for Ross to lead a healthier lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 他们决定要做的第一件事就是让罗斯过上更健康的生活方式。

sentences.en: He basically lived on his computer, so Variety Jones recommended that he take long walks, eat healthier meals and have longer meditation times.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是生活在电脑前，所以“琼斯大杂烩”建议他多散步、吃更健康的饭菜并增加冥想时间。

sentences.en: Ross also decided to leave Australia and head back home.
sentences.zh: 罗斯也决定离开澳大利亚，回到家乡。

sentences.en: On April 10th, 2012, he returned to Austin, Texas.
sentences.zh: 2012年4月10日，他回到了德克萨斯州的奥斯汀。

sentences.en: While Ross was returning to Texas, the investigation into Silk Road by Chicago-based
sentences.zh: 就在罗斯返回德克萨斯州时，芝加哥的国土安全部官员

sentences.zh: 国土安全部

sentences.en: Officer
sentences.zh: 官员

sentences.en: Jared Deryagian was going slower than he would have liked.
sentences.zh: 贾里德·德里亚吉安对丝绸之路的调查进展比他预想的要慢。

sentences.en: He was working on profiling the sellers, but it wasn't easy.
sentences.zh: 他一直在努力为卖家建立档案，但这并不容易。

sentences.en: Every time an envelope with drugs was found by Customs and Border Protection,
sentences.zh: 每当海关和边境保护局发现一个装有毒品的信封时，

sentences.en: Jared would drive to O'Hare Airport to get it, no matter what time of day or night it was.
sentences.zh: 贾里德无论白天还是黑夜，都会开车去奥黑尔机场取件。

sentences.en: Then he would photograph everything, fill out a seizure form and stack it up in his office.
sentences.zh: 然后他会拍下所有东西，填写扣押表格，并把它们堆在办公室里。

sentences.en: By now, he had over 500 different envelopes and he had pictures of the seized drugs stuck all over his walls.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他已经有500多个不同的信封，墙上贴满了缴获毒品的照片。

sentences.en: Once he seized the drug, he went on Silk Road and searched the drugs on display from each seller to see if he could match them to the drugs intercepted by Customs
sentences.zh: 一旦他查获了毒品，他就会登录丝绸之路，搜索每个卖家展示的毒品，看看能否将它们与海关拦截的毒品匹配起来。

sentences.en: and Border Control.
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: All of this took a long time and on top of that, both sellers and buyers at Silk Road were getting smarter.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都需要很长时间，而且最重要的是，丝绸之路上的卖家和买家都变得越来越聪明了。

sentences.en: When it came to buyers, many would use
sentences.zh: 说到买家，许多人会使用

sentences.en: PGP encryption, which turns any text the person enters into an undecipherable block that can only be opened and seen by the person it's addressed to by using a private key.
sentences.zh: PGP加密，它将用户输入的任何文本转换成一个无法破译的区块，只有收件人使用私钥才能打开和查看。

sentences.en: When it came to sellers, they used every imaginable trick to send a drug so they wouldn't be found.
sentences.zh: 说到卖家，他们使用各种可以想象到的诡计来寄送毒品，以免被发现。

sentences.en: One seller put pills inside a hollow marker pen.
sentences.zh: 一位卖家把药丸放在空心的记号笔里。

sentences.en: Another put cocaine inside hollowed-out batteries.
sentences.zh: 另一位把可卡因放在掏空的电池里。

sentences.en: Another put their drugs in the glue behind a shampoo sample inside a magazine.
sentences.zh: 还有一位把毒品藏在杂志里洗发水小样背后的胶水里。

sentences.en: Heroin was often sent folded inside some sheets of A4 paper in an envelope disguised as coming from either a real estate agent, a bank, or a travel agent.
sentences.zh: 海洛因通常被折叠在信封里的几张A4纸中，伪装成来自房地产经纪人、银行或旅行社的信件。

sentences.en: It couldn't be detected when touched.
sentences.zh: 触摸时无法检测出来。

sentences.zh: 正如艾琳·奥姆斯比在《丝绸之路》一书中所概述的那样，

sentences.zh: 大多数包裹都通过了海关，但也有一些被拦截了。

sentences.en: This was known to Silk Road sellers and one of them slipped a note inside his envelopes which read,
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路的卖家对此心知肚明，其中一人在他的信封里塞了一张纸条，上面写着：

sentences.en: If you are the intended recipient, please use responsibly.
sentences.zh: “如果你是预期的收件人，请负责任地使用。”

sentences.en: If you are law enforcement, go fuck yourself.
sentences.zh: “如果你是执法人员，去你妈的。”

sentences.en: Sellers on Silk Road had their own secret section in the forums called
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路上的卖家在论坛里有他们自己的秘密版块，叫做

sentences.en: The Vendors Roundtable.
sentences.zh: “卖家圆桌会议”。

sentences.en: In order to become a part of the Vendors Roundtable, a seller needed to have proven qualifications, which meant they required a good sales record over a certain period of time.
sentences.zh: 为了成为“卖家圆桌会议”的一员，卖家需要有经过验证的资质，这意味着他们需要在一段时间内有良好的销售记录。

sentences.en: In the Vendors Roundtable forum, sellers gave tips to one another on how to hide their drugs and which method worked best for what.
sentences.zh: 在“卖家圆桌会议”论坛中，卖家们互相交流如何隐藏毒品以及哪种方法最有效。

sentences.en: They would also discuss ways to make sales more swiftly and other things to make life easier for them all.
sentences.zh: 他们还会讨论如何更迅速地完成销售，以及其他能让大家生活更轻松的事情。

sentences.en: They understood that they were competing with each other but at the same time, they were also part of a community and when one of them won, everyone won.
sentences.zh: 他们明白彼此之间存在竞争，但同时他们也是社区的一部分，当其中一人获胜时，每个人都获胜。

sentences.en: So they didn't mind helping each other out.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不介意互相帮助。

sentences.en: Another issue that discussed in the Vendors Roundtable was the presence of suspicious buyers.
sentences.zh: “卖家圆桌会议”中讨论的另一个问题是可疑买家的存在。

sentences.en: Buyers who threatened sellers requesting more drugs or they'd give bad feedback and buyers who gave off what they called bad law enforcement vibes.
sentences.zh: 那些威胁卖家要求更多毒品否则就给差评的买家，以及那些散发出他们所谓的“执法部门气息”的买家。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that sellers helped each other out on the forum, they also took precautions.
sentences.zh: 尽管卖家在论坛上互相帮助，但他们也采取了预防措施。

sentences.en: If a seller wanted to make a purchase of their own from Silk Road, they always created a separate buyer account.
sentences.zh: 如果卖家想在丝绸之路进行自己的购买，他们总是会创建一个单独的买家账户。

sentences.en: Although most Silk Road sellers respected one another, giving your address away to a fellow dealer was never a good idea.
sentences.zh: 虽然大多数丝绸之路的卖家互相尊重，但把你的地址告诉同行从来都不是个好主意。

sentences.en: All in all, the Silk Road community was becoming more professional as it grew.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，丝绸之路社区随着规模的扩大变得越来越专业。

sentences.en: It continued to generate more press as well.
sentences.zh: 它也继续产生更多的媒体报道。

sentences.en: Since that first article appeared in Gawker one year earlier,
sentences.zh: 自从一年前那篇报道首次出现在Gawker上以来，

sentences.en: Silk Road was now being covered repeatedly by networks such as NPR,
sentences.zh: 丝绸之路现在被NPR、ABC等多个网络反复报道。

sentences.en: It wasn't filled with the dropkicks and trolls they were expecting.
sentences.zh: 这里并没有他们预想中充斥着混混和喷子。

sentences.en: There were well-thought-out intellectual posts, discussions, debates and even forum threads dedicated to charity.
sentences.zh: 这里有深思熟虑的知识性帖子、讨论、辩论，甚至还有专门用于慈善的论坛主题。

sentences.en: There were discussions about harm minimisation that a doctor participated in.
sentences.zh: 还有医生参与的关于减少伤害的讨论。

sentences.en: There were posts from terminal cancer patients thanking the Dread Pirate Roberts for creating a place where they could get access to cannabis to help live out
sentences.zh: 还有来自癌症晚期患者的帖子，感谢“恐怖海盗罗伯茨”创造了一个让他们可以获得大麻的地方，帮助他们更平静地度过

sentences.en: their days more peacefully.
sentences.zh: 余生。

sentences.en: Posts from people who said their use of drugs was much safer now thanks to Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 还有来自人们的帖子，说多亏了丝绸之路，他们现在使用毒品的方式安全多了。

sentences.en: It was becoming a thriving community.
sentences.zh: 它正在成为一个繁荣的社区。

sentences.en: It was by no means a place filled with just crackheads and criminals.
sentences.zh: 它绝不是一个只充斥着瘾君子和罪犯的地方。

sentences.en: Homeland Security Officer
sentences.zh: 国土安全部官员

sentences.en: Jared Der Yagian saw all of this and he was worried about the slow progress of his investigation while Silk Road was only getting bigger, brighter and better by the day.
sentences.zh: 贾里德·德里亚吉安看到了这一切，他担心自己的调查进展缓慢，而丝绸之路却一天比一天更大、更亮、更好。

sentences.en: He also worried that if more people were finding out about the site then more law enforcement agencies would want to build a case to shut it down.
sentences.zh: 他还担心，如果更多人发现了这个网站，那么更多的执法机构就会想要立案将其关闭。

sentences.en: And he wasn't wrong.
sentences.zh: 他并没有错。

sentences.en: There were already other agencies trying to build cases on Silk Road as detailed in the book
sentences.zh: 正如《美国大亨》一书中所述，已经有其他机构试图对丝绸之路进行立案调查。

sentences.en: American Kingpin.
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: Jared found out about it one afternoon in June 2012.
sentences.zh: 贾里德在2012年6月的一个下午发现了这一点。

sentences.en: He was sitting in his office going through some envelopes when he heard a beeping sound coming from his computer.
sentences.zh: 他坐在办公室里检查一些信封时，听到电脑发出哔哔声。

sentences.en: It was a notification that someone was reading his case.
sentences.zh: 那是有人正在阅读他的案件的通知。

sentences.en: When he checked who, he saw that it was two agents from the Homeland Security
sentences.zh: 当他查看是谁时，发现是来自巴尔的摩国土安全部办公室的两名特工。

sentences.en: Very soon after that,
sentences.zh: 在那之后不久，

sentences.zh: 贾里德的上司收到一封电子邮件，称巴尔的摩的特工正前往芝加哥讨论丝绸之路案件，并且他们还带来了他们的美国检察官。

sentences.en: Jared and his supervisor agreed to the meeting.
sentences.zh: 贾里德和他的上司同意了这次会面。

sentences.en: The meeting didn't involve much of a discussion.
sentences.zh: 会议并没有涉及太多的讨论。

sentences.en: The agents from Baltimore explained that they had turned a dealer who had given them a list of names that belonged to sellers on Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 来自巴尔的摩的特工解释说，他们已经策反了一名毒贩，该毒贩给了他们一份属于丝绸之路卖家的名单。

sentences.en: They planned to go after those sellers and they were certain that one of the names they had belonged to the owner of Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 他们计划追查那些卖家，并且确信他们掌握的名字中有一个属于丝绸之路的所有者。

sentences.en: Jared told the Baltimore agents they were making it sound way too easy.
sentences.zh: 贾里德告诉巴尔的摩的特工，他们把事情说得太简单了。

sentences.en: They had no idea what they were dealing with and they had no respect for Tor or for Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道自己在处理什么，而且他们对Tor或比特币毫无尊重。

sentences.en: Jared was shut down by the US attorney from Baltimore who told him that
sentences.zh: 贾里德被来自巴尔的摩的美国检察官打断了，对方告诉他：

sentences.en: Baltimore would be leading the investigation but he was welcome to help if he had something important to add.
sentences.zh: 巴尔的摩将领导这项调查，但如果他有什么重要的补充，欢迎提供帮助。

sentences.en: Jared's supervisor responded,
sentences.zh: 贾里德的上司回应道：

sentences.en: Here's what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: “我们要这样做。”
